extracted.intended_audience: diagnostic assay developers, clinical laboratorians, and grant reviewers working on lateral flow immunoassays for infectious diseases
extracted.subtask_description: Development, analytical/clinical validation, manufacturing, and biosafety procedures for a lateral flow immunoassay (LFI) to detect Burkholderia pseudomallei capsular polysaccharide (CPS). Covers membrane and reagent selection, GMP production, analytical sensitivity/specificity/reproducibility, stability, field validation, and select-agent biosafety controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membrane selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Membranes will be screened based on their pore size, flow rate, and consistency. Also, nitrocellulose must be converted from a hydrophobic to hydrophilic membrane through treatment with surfactant formulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate a variety of nitrocellulose membranes from multiple sources; choose membranes by pore size/flow/consistency and apply surfactant treatments to render hydrophilic for assay performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test line monoclonal antibody (mAb) selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeating epitopes on CPS allows use of the same mAb for the conjugate and the immobilized test line mAb. Using different mAbs for the conjugate and test line that bind to different epitopes may improve sensitivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider both same-mAb and heterologous mAb pairings; test alternative anti-CPS mAbs to optimize sensitivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absorbent pad function and design
rubrics_metrics.description: The only function of the absorbent pad is to serve as a sink for the liquid processed through the LFI. The size and composition of the absorbent pad will be adjusted following a determination of the sample size needed to achieve sensitivity targets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust pad size/composition based on required sample volume and target sensitivity; tune to sample throughput and flow characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: GMP manufacturing controls and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: InBios manufacturing processes are clearly defined, controlled and documented. All critical processes are validated to ensure consistency and compliance with design specifications. All operators are trained to complete and document procedures. Deviations are investigated and documented. Records of manufactured goods are retained in an accessible form, which enables the complete history of a batch to be traced. The entire InBios manufacturing staff is trained for GMP practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain validated, controlled processes, operator training, deviation handling, traceable batch records, and a trained manufacturing team (engineer, wet chemistry specialists, assemblers) as part of GMP compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit of Detection (LOD) definition and protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: LOD is the concentration of CPS that yields a positive result 50% of the time and a negative result 50% of the time. We will follow the LOD protocol established by the Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute (CLSI) entitled, User Protocol for Evaluation for Qualitative Test Performance. LOD will be determined on GMP produced LFIs; run a number of replicates to accurately determine the LOD for each sample type; determine LOD for CPS spiked into blood, serum and urine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow CLSI qualitative LOD protocol on GMP lots, perform sufficient replicates, evaluate relevant clinical matrices (blood, serum, urine) and use collaborators for matrices not available locally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Deki Readers for quantitative capture of LFI data
rubrics_metrics.description: Deki Readers (Fio corporation) will be implemented; the Deki Reader is a CE marked medical device that can read LFI test strips, digitally captures LFI test and control line data and mobile Fionet software stores test results in a secure cloud network.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deploy Deki Readers at test sites (InBios, UNR, Menzies, Mahidol) to facilitate objective interpretation and centralized storage of LFI results; see commercialization plan for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical reactivity and specificity testing against isolate panels
rubrics_metrics.description: Test 4C4 AMD LFI and alternative mAbs against large panels of B. pseudomallei, B. mallei, and near-neighbor strains, plus clinically relevant bacteria and selected biothreats. Acquire panels from collaborators (CDC/DHS, Keim lab) to establish analytical reactivity and specificity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use extensive isolate panels (example: 77 B. pseudomallei, 33 B. mallei, 36 near neighbors, plus community/hospital bacteria and 7 biothreats); document positives/negatives and cross-reactivity; test large numbers at endemic sites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical reproducibility study design (multi-site)
rubrics_metrics.description: Three sites will be used to test the reproducibility of each optimized LFI lot; Deki Readers will quantify results. Reproducibility studies shall be performed according to CLSI EP15-A2 (User Verification of Performance for Precision and Trueness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare panels in relevant analyte‑negative matrices containing CPS at concentrations that represent assay specification; include high negative, low positive and moderate positive samples; provide positive and negative controls; require concordant results at each site prior to pre-clinical use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precision data analysis methods
rubrics_metrics.description: The Reproducibility (Precision) study uses a QC panel tested at various sites by multiple users. Precision is analyzed by following NCCLS guideline EP5-T2, 'Evaluation of Precision Performance of Clinical Chemistry Devices'. This will establish within-run, day-to-day, site-to-site and total standard deviations and coefficients of variation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute SDs and CVs for within-run, between-day, between-site, and total precision per EP5-T2; use multi-user/site QC panels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ruggedness testing protocol and parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Ruggedness testing shall examine behavior resulting from small changes in environmental and/or operating conditions such as temperature of samples/reagents, accuracy of sample quantity, time to test once collected, sample throughput rate and time to result, reagent concentration, age of reagents, mixing time, temperature of analysis, flow rates, variations in measuring apparatus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have a detailed protocol describing parameters to be studied; evaluate QC panels comparing ruggedness-perturbed tests to control group; analyze with paired Student's t-tests to assess significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stability and shelf-life testing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical shelf life for rapid tests prepared with the proposed LFI format is 24 months at room temperature but depends on active components. Final assay design shall be evaluated using three different lots of test strips according to the same SOP. Reagent shelf life is measured by a combination of real-time and accelerated stability testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform real-time and accelerated aging on multiple production lots, evaluate QC panels versus control and expected values, and analyze results with paired Student's t-tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field validation at endemic sites and comparison to gold standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Validate AMD LFI in field studies at two geographical sites using archived sera and other matrices to confirm diagnostic algorithm and compare with appropriate gold standard for melioidosis confirmation (culture). Also compare with commonly used rapid techniques (PCR, IFA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distribute a large lot of LFIs to endemic sites (e.g., Mahidol, MSHR), test de-identified culture-confirmed and sepsis patient samples, and methodically compare LFI results to culture and two rapid diagnostics used regionally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical sample size and sampling expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaborators estimate a minimum of 300 culture-confirmed melioidosis cases per year in endemic regions; an average of three patient sample types are collected from each patient, yielding ~900 samples to be evaluated. Mahidol has at least 1000 suspected cases/year with ~100 culture-confirmed; MSHR confirmed 254 cases over 2.5 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan sample acquisition logistics and statistical power around expected case rates; leverage archived samples and multi-matrix sampling (blood, urine, pus, respiratory secretions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation and reporting of sensitivity and specificity and cross-reactivity
rubrics_metrics.description: All results shall be expressed in a specificity table summarizing analysis of normal samples and cross-reactivity. The % sensitivity and % specificity will be calculated based on the number of AMD-positive or negative samples that correlated with culture positive or negative data. AMD-positive/culture-negative cases may represent 'clinical melioidosis' and should be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate statistical methods for analysis; document and investigate discordant AMD-positive/culture-negative results per published diagnostic criteria (e.g., Limmathurotsakul); include cross-reactivity tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product specification and performance targets
rubrics_metrics.description: Product Specification: Active Melioidosis Detect™ (AMD; LFI). Intended Use: in vitro diagnosis of active melioidosis for visual and rapid qualitative detection of CPS. Analytes: whole blood (venous/capillary), plasma/serum, urine, pus, respiratory secretions. Detection agent: selected antibody(s) to CPS conjugated with gold. Buffer: chase buffer that should not require cold storage. No additional instrumentation required. Performance input: sensitivity targets by matrix (Pus >98%, Sputum >98%, Urine >95%, Blood >90%), Specificity ≥95%, Analytical sensitivity LOD ≤1 ng/ml, Comparative methods: PCR, IFA, Culture, Reading time 5–20 minutes, Shelf life 24 months at RT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design device and documentation to meet these matrix-specific sensitivity targets, specificity threshold, LOD goal, non-refrigerated buffer, rapid time-to-result, and comparative method equivalency to culture/PCR/IFA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matrix comparison study requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Matrix comparison for serum/plasma, whole blood (venous/capillary), urine, pus, and respiratory secretions will be compared. Spike purified CPS and/or CPS-containing clinical samples into matrices at concentrations close to LOD and test to determine which matrix or matrices are most suitable for the current LFI format. Results will be reported in the FDA application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform in-house or collaborator-based matrix spike studies near LOD for each candidate matrix; document matrix effects and select optimal matrices for clinical use and regulatory submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations and contingency/alternative strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: If major problems arise (high false positive rates, poor sensitivity, etc.) then InBios will make proper modifications to the LFI and produce additional GMP lots for testing. Sample preparation guidelines may be modified if needed during larger LFI analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan iterative redesign and repeat GMP lot production if performance targets are not met; adjust sample prep protocols as an alternative mitigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantification of CPS expression and secretion (qCPS ELISA studies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use qCPS ELISA to establish concentration of CPS within in vitro cultures, de-identified patient samples, and samples from animals challenged via aerosol route. Determine variation of CPS expression across a diverse panel of B. pseudomallei isolates and perform time-course sampling; quantify CPS per bacterial cell and CPS/ml using purified CPS standard curve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select isolates representing major clades, grow cultures, perform quantitative cultures and qCPS ELISA against purified CPS standards to map expression/secretion profiles across genetic diversity and infection time courses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation in animal aerosol models (mouse and NHP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate 4C4 AMD LFI with BALB/c mice and rhesus macaque aerosol challenge studies; collect urine, blood and oral swabs prior to and following infection at defined time points. Provide qCPS ELISA reagents to collaborators to quantify CPS in collected samples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pilot and full animal studies should include pre- and post-infection timepoints, compare qCPS ELISA concentrations to LFI results, and test as many samples as volumes permit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correlation of qCPS ELISA with culture and handling of culture-negative/CPS-positive samples
rubrics_metrics.description: Filtered urine and serum samples analyzed with qCPS ELISA showed detectable CPS in some samples; anticipate detection of higher CPS when whole bacterial cells are not removed by filtration. Culture (CFU/ml) data will be compared with CPS concentration. Blood and urine samples that are culture negative from melioidosis positive patients will be evaluated for CPS presence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ship de-identified samples to BSL-3 lab for ELISA; compare CPS concentration to culture results, and interpret CPS-positive/culture-negative findings as possible shed antigen from abscesses or distant sites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate detection approaches for low CPS concentrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential problems with low CPS concentrations in blood may be addressed with use of mAb 4C4 instead of mAb 3C5 in the qCPS ELISA. Additionally, use of SPR (linking mAb 4C4 to SPR sensor chip) can detect far lower concentrations with small sample volumes (~10 µl).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have contingency plans to switch capture/detection mAbs and to deploy higher-sensitivity techniques (SPR) for samples with very low antigen concentrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subjects protections for archived sample use
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies will utilize only archived and commercial human samples without personal identifiers. Subjects will not be selected based on age or ethnicity; fetuses, neonates, pregnant women, prisoners or institutionalized individuals will not be used. Request Exemption 4. Samples are de-identified and used under existing consent for diagnostic studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use archived de-identified samples, adhere to DHHS/NIH regulations (45 CFR 46.102(f)), follow local IRB/consent constraints, and ensure universal precautions in handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion policy for women and minorities
rubrics_metrics.description: No selection/exclusion based on sex or racial/ethnic group; archived samples will include male/female and ethnically diverse individuals reflective of sample origin demographics. No specific outreach will be done because samples are archived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document sample demographics and rationales for inclusion; ensure archived sample sets reasonably reflect endemic population diversity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of children
rubrics_metrics.description: Archived samples will include children; special recruitment of children will not take place. Children are not excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include pediatric archived specimens where available; ensure appropriate de-identification and ethical handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select Agent registration and facility description requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide registration status of all entities where Select Agent (B. pseudomallei and B. mallei) will be used. Work will be done in newly constructed CDC-certified BSL-3 laboratory within the Center for Molecular Medicine; BSL-3 designed/constructed for Select Agent use and certified through consultation with experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain and report formal Select Agent registration numbers, describe certified facilities, ensure BSL-3 design/performance meets NIH/BMBL requirements, and document oversight/consultation used in commissioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select Agent inventory, access control and record-keeping
rubrics_metrics.description: Records of all B. pseudomallei and all Select Agent possession will be maintained in inventory logs. A Select Agent suite contains a locked Select Agent freezer; access allowed only to select agent approved employees. Inventory logs note user name, agent, dates/times removed/returned, purpose of use, and date/method of disposal. Monthly/quarterly inventories are performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement locked storage, strict access control, per-use logging, periodic inventory reconciliation, and locked documentation accessible only to approved personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosafety, biocontainment and operational procedures for select agent work
rubrics_metrics.description: All work with viable B. pseudomallei will take place in the CMM BSL-3. Open cultures will be handled within biosafety cabinets. Biosafety Class II cabinets used with HEPA filtration; negative pressure ventilation functional. PPE including powered air-purifying respirators (PAPR) required for open culture work. All reusable equipment decontaminated; materials to be discarded autoclaved and sterilization verified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow BSL-3 operational protocols: use certified cabinets, HEPA filtration, negative pressure, appropriate PPE, routine autoclaving/decontamination, and verification of sterilization; document procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security measures for BSL-3 and Select Agent containment
rubrics_metrics.description: Security measures include eight video surveillance cameras monitored centrally, no outside-facing windows, card-key access with pass-code, real-time logging of entries/exits, designation of Select Agent suite and locked -80°C freezer with combination lock, and prohibition of 'piggy-backing' and unaccompanied visitors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement layered physical security (surveillance, controlled access, logging), enforce individual access, secure storage for agents, and policies preventing unauthorized entry; maintain logs for investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Destruction and disposal documentation for Select Agents
rubrics_metrics.description: All materials to be discarded will be autoclaved at the end of every work session and the sterilization verified. Other reusable equipment will be decontaminated at the end of every work session. Destruction/disposal of the Select Agents is documented on a log sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record autoclave cycles and verification, document decontamination of reusable equipment, and maintain disposal logs for regulatory compliance.
